pr.title: Make sure we handle `backwards_incompatible_lint` drops appropriately in drop elaboration
pr.description:
In #131326, a new kind of scheduled drop (`drop_kind: DropKind::Value` + `backwards_incompatible_lint: true`) was added so that we could insert a new kind of no-op MIR statement (`backward incompatible drop`) for linting purposes. 

These drops were intended to have *no side-effects*, but drop elaboration code forgot to handle these drops specially and they were handled otherwise as normal drops in most of the code. This ends up being **unsound** since we insert more than one drop call for some values, which means that `Drop::drop` could be called more than once.

This PR fixes this by splitting out the `DropKind::ForLint` and adjusting the code. I'm not totally certain if all of the places I've adjusted are either reachable or correct, but I'm pretty certain that it's *more* correct than it was previously.

cc @dingxiangfei2009 
r? nikomatsakis

Fixes #134482

issues.title: Double Drop with #![deny(rust_2024_compatibility)]
issues.body:
I had a custom Rc that was doubly freeing memory because Drop was being called more times than it should. After a little bit of testing I think this is a small enough Minimal-Reproducible-Example: [playground](https://play.rust-lang.org/?version=nightly&mode=debug&edition=2021&gist=4943de32dc0785a67a3f78b5ce9a478b) ```rust // ---------------------------------------- // // If commented, it only calls Drop 2 times // // If not commented, it calls Drop 3 times // // ---------------------------------------- // #![deny(rust_2024_compatibility)] use std::backtrace::Backtrace; struct Guard(); impl Clone for Guard { fn clone(&self) -> Self { Self() } } impl Drop for Guard { fn drop(&mut self) { println!("Drop!"); eprintln!("Drop at {}!", Backtrace::force_capture()); } } fn main() { let _ = method_1(Guard()); } fn method_1(g: Guard) -> Result { // ----------------------- // // This calls Drop 2 times // // ----------------------- // // let argument = &g.clone(); // match method_2(argument) { // Ok(str) => Ok(str), // Err(err) => Err(err), // } // --- // // ----------------------- // // This calls Drop 3 times // // ----------------------- // match method_2(&g.clone()) { Ok(str) => Ok(str), Err(err) => Err(err), } } fn method_2(_: &Guard) -> Result { panic!("Method 2 panics!"); } ``` I expected to see this happen: Drop is called twice. Instead, this happened: Drop is called 3 times. ### Notes * The return type doesn't need to be a `Result` It seems that it happens as long as it is an enum in which one arm has a non-`Copy` type. So it also happens if the return type is ```rust enum CustomEnum { MyArm(Vec), } ``` * The problems seems to happen regardless of the presence of the `--release` flag * As seen in the backtrace below, the first drop is called at the end of the enum match, and the other two are called at the end of method_1 ### Meta `rustc --version --verbose`: ``` rustc 1.85.0-nightly (a4cb3c831 2024-12-17) binary: rustc commit-hash: a4cb3c831823d9baa56c3d90514b75b2660116fa commit-date: 2024-12-17 host: x86_64-pc-windows-msvc release: 1.85.0-nightly LLVM version: 19.1.5 ```
Backtrace

Reduced stderr from the playground: ``` Running `target/debug/playground` thread 'main' panicked at src/main.rs:51:5: Method 2 panics! note: run with `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` environment variable to display a backtrace Drop at 0: ::drop at ./src/main.rs:18:33 1: core::ptr::drop_in_place at ./.rustup/toolchains/nightly-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/lib/rustlib/src/rust/library/core/src/ptr/mod.rs:522:1 2: playground::method_1 at ./src/main.rs:46:5 3: [...] Drop at 0: ::drop at ./src/main.rs:18:33 1: core::ptr::drop_in_place at ./.rustup/toolchains/nightly-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/lib/rustlib/src/rust/library/core/src/ptr/mod.rs:522:1 2: playground::method_1 at ./src/main.rs:47:1 3: [...] Drop at 0: ::drop at ./src/main.rs:18:33 1: core::ptr::drop_in_place at ./.rustup/toolchains/nightly-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/lib/rustlib/src/rust/library/core/src/ptr/mod.rs:522:1 2: playground::method_1 at ./src/main.rs:47:1 3: [...] ```

analysis.summary: In Rust's ElaborateDrops pass, lint-only "backward incompatible drop" hints were scheduled as ordinary value drops (DropKind::Value plus a backwards_incompatible_lint flag) and thus handled as normal drops in several drop-elaboration paths. That emitted real drop calls for a lint-only no-op, causing duplicate Drop::drop invocations and unsoundness. The fix introduces DropKind::ForLint and handles it specially wherever drops are built/elaborated, emitting only BackwardIncompatibleDropHint statements.
analysis.originalLogic: Scheduled drops had DropKind::Value or DropKind::Storage plus a separate `backwards_incompatible_lint: bool` field. A lint-only scheduled drop was represented as `DropKind::Value` with `backwards_incompatible_lint: true`, intended to insert the no-op MIR statement `BackwardIncompatibleDropHint` for linting only. The PR description states: "a new kind of scheduled drop (`drop_kind: DropKind::Value` + `backwards_incompatible_lint: true`) was added so that we could insert a new kind of no-op MIR statement (`backward incompatible drop`) for linting purposes."
analysis.incorrectTransformation: Because the lint drop's `kind` remained `DropKind::Value`, most drop-elaboration code handled it as an ordinary value drop, inserting actual `TerminatorKind::Drop` calls in addition to the hint. The PR says: "These drops were intended to have *no side-effects*, but drop elaboration code forgot to handle these drops specially and they were handled otherwise as normal drops in most of the code. This ends up being **unsound** since we insert more than one drop call for some values, which means that `Drop::drop` could be called more than once." The fix "splitting out the `DropKind::ForLint` and adjusting the code" gives lint-only drops their own kind so they emit only `StatementKind::BackwardIncompatibleDropHint` rather than real drop terminators.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR drop elaboration for Rust functions compiled with a backwards-incompatible drop lint active (for example `#![deny(tail_expr_drop_order)]` / edition-2024 compatibility). The function must contain a value whose drop is scheduled only to support the lint, and surrounding control flow that causes drop elaboration to process that scheduled drop, including normal and unwind paths. The reported repro is a tail expression `match method_2(&g.clone())` over a `Result` whose `Ok` arm contains a non-Copy type with a `Drop` impl, while another value (`Guard`) is also dropped. A variant that binds `let argument = &g.clone();` first and does not have the tail-expression lint drop does not exhibit the duplicate drop.
analysis.trigger: A lint-only scheduled drop (originally `DropKind::Value` plus `backwards_incompatible_lint: true`) is elaborated into a real drop, especially on unwind/cleanup paths where the drop tree or `build_scope_drops` treats it like a normal value drop. The hint statement is then emitted alongside one or more actual `drop(...)` terminators for the same local. The issue reports: "I expected to see this happen: Drop is called twice." followed by "Instead, this happened: Drop is called 3 times."
preconditions: Drop elaboration is running on MIR containing a backwards-incompatible lint drop, e.g. a scheduled drop for `tail_expr_drop_order` under `#![deny(tail_expr_drop_order)]`.
The lint-only drop is represented with the ordinary value-drop kind rather than a distinct lint kind, so drop-tree construction and unwind adjustment treat it as a side-effecting drop.
There is also a real value whose destructor is scheduled/dropped around the same control flow, so duplicate drop elaboration produces an observable extra `Drop::drop` call.
The function includes a match/tail expression over a non-Copy enum payload, plus an unwind path such as a panicking call.
pitfalls: Do not represent a lint-only no-op drop as `DropKind::Value`; give it a distinct kind (`DropKind::ForLint`) so all drop-elaboration code can avoid emitting a real `Drop` terminator.
A lint drop must emit only `StatementKind::BackwardIncompatibleDropHint`; emitting `TerminatorKind::Drop` for it is unsound because `Drop::drop` can run multiple times.

When adjusting `unwind_to` for `DropKind::ForLint` in `build_scope_drops`, only advance it when `storage_dead_on_unwind` is true; normally lint-related drops are not emitted on unwind, so leaving `unwind_to` unchanged is intentional.

Moved-local elision for lint drops: in `build_scope_drops`, if the local appears in `scope.moved_locals` and this is not an unwind path, skip generating the hint. The code comments that this is done 'so as not to disturb the caching mechanism.'
`needs_cleanup` must treat both `DropKind::Value` and `DropKind::ForLint` as needing cleanup, while `DropKind::Storage` does not.
Use `DUMMY_SP` for the terminator/source info on lint-only paths so debuginfo does not place breakpoints there, especially on unwind paths.

Do not conflate the lint drop's hint statement with a real drop; the MIR test's expected output contains `backward incompatible drop(_2);` and `backward incompatible drop(_5);` in `bb7`, and real drops appear separately.
analysis.testStrategy: Add a mir-opt inline test under `tests/mir-opt/` with `// skip-filecheck`, `// EMIT_MIR_FOR_EACH_PANIC_STRATEGY`, and `// EMIT_MIR tail_expr_drop_order_unwind.method_1.ElaborateDrops.after.mir`. Compile with `#![deny(tail_expr_drop_order)]`, define a `#[derive(Clone)]` type with a `Drop` impl (`Guard`) and another non-Copy `Drop` type (`OtherDrop`), and write a function with the tail expression `match method_2(&g.clone()) { Ok(other_drop) => {...} Err(err) => {} }` where `method_2` panics. Inspect the after-ElaborateDrops MIR to verify each lint-only local receives exactly one `backward incompatible drop(...)` statement and is not also the target of a normal `drop(...)` terminator; compare the panic-abort and panic-unwind expectations. The test comment notes that the repro needs something else being dropped too.

This ends up being **unsound** since we insert more than one drop call for some values, which means that `Drop::drop` could be called more than once.
This PR fixes this by splitting out the `DropKind::ForLint` and adjusting the code.
